dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: My brother §aTeddy §fand I are some of the greatest hunters who have ever lived.

§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: Climb up high, §2Lasso §fin hand, and sneak up on 'em.

§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: Keep an eye on 'em while you get yer §2Lasso §fout.
§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: Don't blink, or they'll come right atcha.
§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: Them frogs known as §aDustybits §fleap around the §6Spring Path§f.
§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: Chase 'em down, following them after each leap, an' eventually they'll get too tired to run any more.
§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: It's a battle of attrition, I'll say, you versus the beast.
§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: Them §aEmbers §flive in §bTorrhus Springs§f, I believe.
§e[NPC] §aFreddy§f: They be quite deep down, compared to §aSolars§f.

§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Hi §7<player>§f!
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: §bDavid Hunterborough §fsays you've completed your training.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Now, it's time to teach you the true purpose of §ahunting§f.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Every Shard you collect goes into your §aHunting Box§f, located in the §aHunting Skill Menu§f.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: There are two things you can do with those Shards.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Are you following so far?
§eSelect an option: §a[Of course!]
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: You can either §csyphon §for §5fuse §fthem.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Syphoning is key - it lets you permanently gain the §cattribute §fof the creature it came from.
§eSelect an option: §a[What are attributes?]
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Attributes are very much like §2Pet §fabilities in a way.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: But hunting lets you harness those powers independently of the creature.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Here, take this Phanpyre Shard.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Open your §aHunting Box§f, inside the §aHunting Skill Menu§f, and §csyphon §fit.
§6Kysha gave you 1x Phanpyre Shard!
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Go inside your §aHunting Box§f, inside the §aHunting Skill Menu§f, and §cSyphon §fit.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Congratulations! You permanently unlocked the §7[Shard Name] §fattribute!
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Every time you §csyphon §fmore of a Shard, that §cattribute §fwill grow stronger.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: You can view it in your §cAttribute Menu §finside the §aHunting Skill Menu§f.
§eSelect an option: §a[Anything else?]
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Yes!
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Like I said earlier, you can also §5fuse §fShards.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: The §5Precursors §fbuilt a machine that merges the genetic essence of two creatures.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: We call this process §5fusion§f.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: To fuse, combine §a5 §fShards of one creature with §a5 §fShards of another in the Fusion Machine.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: The fusion process can uncover creatures that haven't been discovered yet!
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: I've given you §a5 Phanpyre Shards §fand §a5 Cod Shards §fto fuse in the Fusion Machine.
§e[NPC] §bKysha§f: Try it out and see what you can create!
§6Kysha gave you 5x Phanpyre Shards and 5x Cod Shards!

dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Greetings, traveler.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: I'm Loras, a historian dedicated to uncovering the secrets of the §5Precursors§f.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Sadly, their history is shrouded in mystery, with scarce records surviving.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: I've had to piece together their story through fieldwork and ancient relics.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: My dream? To pen a comprehensive tome about them, but the pieces are still falling into place.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Interested in what I've uncovered so far?
§eSelect an option: §a[Yes] §c[Later, maybe]
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Understandable. History has a way of capturing us when we least expect it.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Feel free to return if curiosity strikes.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Ah, a fellow history enthusiast! Excellent.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Through my research, I've deducted that the Precursors were this world's first inhabitants.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Remarkably, they lived under the watch of multiple entities called §9Starborns§f!
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: I've identified at least eight Starborns, but I suspect there were more.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Each Starborn had a unique domain and wielded immense power.
§eSelect an option: §a[What kind of domain?]
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: From the Starborn of the Forests or the Sea, even a Starborn of Life!
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: It's unclear whether the Precursors were creations of these Starborns, but they certainly revered them.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: My studies led me to distinguish two categories: Old and New Starborns.
§eSelect an option: §a[Not very original.]
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Ah, but the names reflect a theory.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: The Old Starborns seemen indifferent to mortal affairs, transcending earthly desires.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Conversely, the New Starborns engaged actively with the Precursors, reveling in their advancements and guiding their progress.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: I believe that immortals who maintain worldly interests and desire could be considered 'young' in a divine sense.
§eSelect an option: §a[It's an interesting theory]
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Much appreciated.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: The New Starborns were particularly invested, almost as proud mentors observing their wards' milestones.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: They even intervened directly at times, teaching essential lessons like substainable living and the imporance of nature's balance.
§eSelect an option: §a[So the Starborns were spectating them]

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Starborns were spectating them]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Precisely, but also guiding.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Starborns were spectating them]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: For instance, they introduced magic to the Precursors, a decision with unforeseen consequences.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Starborns were spectating them]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: The Precursors ended up excelling in both magic and science, eventually blending the two to create wonders.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Starborns were spectating them]
dialogues.raw: §eSelect an option: §a[I see where this is going]

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Their ambition grew boundless.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: They sought more: longer life, greater strength, boundless energy.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Later generations of Precursors, born into a world of accomplishments, yearned for purpose and legacy.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: For those young generations of Precursors, it became impossible to define their own purpose in the shadow of monumental achievements.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Something had to happen, the wheel of progress had to keep turning.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: So one day, a bold claim arose: the Precursors had surpassed the Starborns.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: They saw the Starborns' teachings as shackles, hindering their true potential.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [I see where this is going]
dialogues.raw: §eSelect an option: §a[Those Precursors are very human after all]

dialogues.condition: Selecting [Those Precursors are very human after all]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Indeed... But this hubris marked the beginning of the end.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [Those Precursors are very human after all]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: The Precursors harnessed their tools and magic to overpower the Starborns.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [Those Precursors are very human after all]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Adding to this, the Starborns' power was intrinsically tied to the belief of their followers.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [Those Precursors are very human after all]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: As the Precursors' faith diminished, so too did the might of the Starborns, weakening them in this crucial confrontation.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [Those Precursors are very human after all]
dialogues.raw: §eSelect an option: §a[Can Starborns even die?]
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: That remains a mystery. But it's clear that their influence faded.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: As for the Precursors, they vanished without a trace, a puzzling paradox.
§eSelect an option: §a[So how does the story end?]

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So how does the story end?]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Here's my theory: aware of their impending doom, the Starborn of Time, perhaps the most powerful due to universal belief, made a desperate move.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So how does the story end?]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: He propelled the Precursors far into the future, hoping that by then, others could stand against them.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So how does the story end?]
dialogues.raw: §eSelect an option: §a[The future? When exactly?]
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: That's the unknown.
§e[NPC] §bLoras§f: But it suggests that the Precursors might reemerge one day, a thought both fascinating and daunting.
§eSelect an option: §a[So the Precursors will just appear out of nowhere one day?]

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Precursors will just appear out of nowhere one day?]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: It's a possibility we cannot ignore.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Precursors will just appear out of nowhere one day?]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: We must be prepared for whatever comes.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Precursors will just appear out of nowhere one day?]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Thank you for lending an ear to my life's work.

dialogues.condition: Selecting [So the Precursors will just appear out of nowhere one day?]
dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bLoras§f: Now, I must return to my studies.

§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: Friends of my friends are my enemies - §f§owhoops§f, my friends I mean!
§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: You might be wondering why I'm on top of this bush?
§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: I'm camping it to get the §dberries §fbefore someone else.

§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: A §dberry §fjust appeared, simply §cpunch §fthe bush to collect it!
§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: Great!
§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: §dBerries §fare pretty useful to craft §aHunting §fitems.

§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: Here, let me give you this legendary axe that has been passed down my whole family tree for 12 generations.

§e[NPC] §bSwoop§f: For example, §210∮ Sweep §fshould allow you to cut §e10 logs§f, you understand?

dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §bTalia§f: The view from here is just so bad.
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: I mean look at it! Look!
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: It’s hard to even describe how awful this view is.
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: I come here everyday just to see how terrible this view is.
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: Every time I look, it somehow gets worse!
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: I traveled all the way... just to be disappointed again.
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: This island somehow managed to have an even worse view.
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: Every rock, every tree, perfectly misplaced. It's a masterpiece of disaster.
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: Pure, breathtaking mediocrity.
§e[NPC] §bTalia§f: I could stare at this abomination for hours. Can't wait to come back tomorrow.

dialogues.raw: §e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: I am Teddy, the §f§olegendary §fhunter. Yes, yes, I know what you're thinking... no need to bow.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: I've walked this earth for 152 years, seen every creature, caught every beast... except... anyways.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: I can teach you how to catch anything that walks, swims, or slithers on this island...
§eSelect an option: §a[Wow, thanks!]
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: ...For a price, of course. Nothing in life is free, kiddo.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Struggling with Frogs? Really?
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Back in my day, hunters would catch 'em blindfolded.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Hunters these days... no patience. Go to the lake and look for Mossybits.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Just poke at 'em, and they'll jump like they've seen a ghost. Eventually, they'll tire out.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Easy peasy.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Mudworms? You've gotta watch the ground closely... and I mean closely.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Ever seen a faint glow in the dirt? Could be treasure... or a Mudworm.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Either way, you're digging!
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Ah, the Axolotl, tricky little devils. But here's a secret...
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Their eyesight is rubbish, they only detect movements. So if you stand still long enough near them, you're golden.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Shulkers are sneaky. They're like shadows that play tricks on you.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: There are Hideonleafs on the island.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Step on them by mistake, and, well, they can get quite angry.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: When they attack, smack their projectiles right back at 'em. That'll teach 'em.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Lumisquids hide in awkward places… but that's half the fun, right?
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f:  Use your net on them until they shrink down.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: They'll poof away like magic, but they never go too far.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Dolphins... smart and slippery. They'll flee to their dolphin holes if you're not quick enough.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Get that net ready, and don't stop until you catch up to them. But hurry, they won't wait around for a chat.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Cod? Oh, please. The most boring of fish, hands down.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Spin 'em with a fishing net; they'll twirl like a clumsy dancer.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Spin 'em too much, though, and... well, you'll see.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Pandas? Oh, now we're talking real game!
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: They're tough to find, but this old hunter knows a trick or two.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Feed 'em bamboo, and they might just love you for a second.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: But finding them?
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: That's a secret only a 165-year-old like me can tell you. I won't though.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Salmon? Fast as lightning, those slippery devils.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Hit 'em with the net to slow them down. Just don't blink, or you'll be left with water in your boots.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Ah, the Invisibug, nearly impossible to see... but not to me, of course.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Look for the glow, throw a lasso, and hope your aim's as sharp as mine.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Shellwise, the ancient ones.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Well, ancient compared to you, not me, I'm only 178, after all.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: No real tricks here. Just chuck your net until they give up.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: It's not pretty, but it works.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: Pufferfish... Have you tried looking in the Kelpwoven Tunnels?
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: I've seen a few, Spikes they are called.
§e[NPC] §aTeddy§f: You'll need a special Fishing Net with a long range and stand at a distance from them.

§e[NPC] §2Treehugger Timothy§f: I bet you wanna cut it so bad, right? Get all that loot and everything.
